newsitem.title: GERMANY: ROWING-REDGRAVE'S QUARTET WINS COXLESS FOUR.
newsitem.headline: ROWING-REDGRAVE'S QUARTET WINS COXLESS FOUR.

text.p: The new British coxless four of Olympic champions Steve Redgrave and Matthew Pinsent with Tim Foster and James Cracknell won their final convincingly in the first regatta of the new Rowing World Cup which finished on Sunday at the Olympic course.
The quartet, who continue to improve with every race, were pleased with their success as they continue to build towards the 2000 Olympics in Sydney.

Redgrave, the four times Olympic gold medallist, said afterwards: "The World Cup is a big thing for us. Winning here has put us in the driving seat for the season and we know we can go faster. We want to win every race in every regatta we go to."
Host nation Germany took the overall title by winning five of the 14 classes as a strong head wind again caused problems with crews drawn in the outside lanes battling difficult conditions.
The German successes came in the men's quadruple sculls, the lightweight men's double sculls, the men's eights, the women's double sculls and the women's quadruple sculls.
Britain finished second overall with one win and two second places with Denmark in third place with two victories.
Former world champion Iztok Cop of Slovenia won the men's single sculls ahead of Egypt's Ibrahim Ali, who became the first rower from the African continent to win a major international regatta medal.
Jamie Koven, a member of the Americans' world champion eight in 1984, finished third in his first season in the single sculls.
Double Olympic quadruple sculls champion Andre Willms of Germany surprisingly finished last but undoubtedly suffered from his outside lane draw.

Olympic champion Katya Khodotovich of Belarus comfortably won the women's single sculls ahead of Atlanta bronze medallist Trine Hansen of Denmark. Maria Brandin of Sweden pushed hard in the last 500 metres but had to settle for third place.

Matt Smith, Executive Director of the International Rowing Federation (FISA), commented: "Our goals were to produce a top series of events outside our World Championships, thus providing world class competition for our athletes, and to promote our sport. We have achieved the first and made huge strides forward with the second. This really is the beginning of a new era for rowing."
The next regatta in the series is in Paris from June 20-22 with the final regatta in Lucerne, Switzerland, from July 11-13.
